attempts.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as a NAT egress router for node2/node3 (RHEL10), implemented entirely via an Ansible playbook run from node4 (the cluster's Ansible control node). node1's eth1 (aliased enp8s0) got a static private-subnet address (10.50.50.254/24) plus a source-NAT masquerade rule on eth0 for 10.50.50.0/24. node2/node3 got static addresses (10.50.50.11/.12) on their second NIC with node1 as gateway (lower-priority default route, metric 200, alongside their existing primary-network route), plus rp_filter=0 on that NIC to stop the kernel dropping NAT-returned replies that arrive asymmetrically relative to the primary route. Verified end-to-end egress (ping + HTTPS) from both private clients through node1's NAT. All four managed nodes (node1-4) were then restarted one at a time per the mandatory protocol, with boot_id captured before/after each restart and full functional/config recovery confirmed afterward (NAT rule, static IPs, rp_filter setting, and live internet reachability through NAT all persisted across node1's reboot).
